requirements.statement: An empty generation configuration remains usable and preserves the existing field prefix, empty class overrides, and unset project/package overrides.
A supported local OpenAPI document produces the corresponding model, endpoint, and client Python files, and those generated files remain syntactically compilable.
An invalid local OpenAPI document returns an explicit parsing error without leaving an apparently successful generated package.
Unsupported OpenAPI major versions remain explicitly rejected without leaving an apparently successful generated project.
The input document and optional generation configuration retain their existing control over project name, package name, and generated version.
Required input schema fields retain their required meaning in generated models.
Omittable input schema fields retain the existing distinction between an omitted value and a supplied value in generated models.
Nullable input schema fields retain their existing allowance for null without conflating null with an omitted value.
Generated model dictionary input and output preserve the original schema field names even when their Python identifiers differ.
Cross-component schema references and references used by endpoints resolve to the corresponding generated model rather than an unrelated or missing type.
Generated model code remains importable and its existing from_dict and to_dict protocol can execute on supported document inputs while preserving the corresponding field values.
Generated endpoint code remains importable and preserves the existing path assembly and response parsing behavior without requiring a request to a remote service for validation.
Generation modes that produce project metadata continue rendering the complete corresponding project metadata alongside models, client, and endpoints.
The generation workflow continues invoking the existing formatting commands for the generated project, without replacing them with a no-op.

The application runs in the registered new dependency environment through native Pydantic v2 APIs; routing the migrated application through pydantic.v1 or retaining the old Pydantic runtime is not an accepted migration.
The migration changes only registered application Python files and preserves the original templates, checks, dependency locks, and business contract.
